items.title: Leonard Bocage Interview, 1972-03-24
items.q: I played with his daddy... Percy, Percy Umphrey... I played with all of them.

ctx.x: Then I played in the, uh, I played with his daddy. I played in the brass band. I played bass drum with his daddy in the brass band. Mm-hmm. And after I left his daddy, I started playing with the Excelsior Brass Band. Started playing bass drum with the Excelsior Brass Band. Mm-hmm. Well, my cousin Peter was leader of the Excelsior Brass Band at that time. Mm-hmm. And they had, uh, Peter on trumpet, George McCullen on trumpet, Charlie Love on trumpet, and Percy, Percy Umphrey. Willie Umphrey on clarinet. Uh,…
Henry is kin to you, too, now.

items.title: Leonard Bocage Interview, 1972-03-24
items.q: This old man had some nice marches back there, and I knew at that time... He used to have first-class marches.

ctx.x: We could have... Yeah, go ahead.
The old man couldn't ever play nothing about head, but he was a good reader, the old man. He could read, but he couldn't play nothing about head.
Did you ever hear him play, Yes, Lord, I'm Cripple?
